Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
9:01 PM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying someone as easy as sending a message. You open any payment app, scan a code or pick a contact, enter an amount and your PIN, and the money moves from bank to bank in seconds. There is no card machine, no cash to count and no change to hunt for.

It also works everywhere. A tea stall, a vegetable seller, a large store and a friend who owes you for dinner can all be paid the same way. Small shops especially like it, since they only need a printed code to start accepting money.

The main reasons people give:

Free and instant: Most everyday payments cost nothing, and the money arrives straight away, even on holidays and late at night.
Simple and widely accepted: One code or phone number works across every bank and app, from big shops to street vendors.
Easy to start: All you need is a bank account linked to your phone number. No card or special device is required.

Habit has done the rest. Once people see friends, family and local shops using UPI, carrying cash starts to feel like extra effort. Bills, rent, recharges and online orders have also moved to it, so there is one familiar way to pay for nearly everything. Safety features such as the PIN and instant alerts from your bank add to the comfort.
